commendātĭcĭus or -tĭus , a, um, adj. commendatio,
I.serving for commendation, commendatory (very rare): litterae, letters of recommendation or introduction, Cic. Fam. 5, 5, 1; cf. Dig. 41, 1, 65; so, “tabellae,” Cic. Verr. 2, 4, 66, § 148 ; and absol., commendaticiae, ārum, f., Aug. in Macr. S. 2, 4, 15.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
